description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p09-delete-addr.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 2 rows):
  delete.t 26 `a b c equivalent`         (hash spelling, perl-tests/delete.t:79)
  delete.t 54 `a b c also equivalent`    (array spelling, :153)

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    { my %a = ('bar', 33);
      my ($a) = \(values %a); my $b = \$a{bar}; my $c = \delete $a{bar};
      printf "hash: ab=%d bc=%d\n", ($a==$b)?1:0, ($b==$c)?1:0; }
    { my @a = 33;
      my ($a) = \(@a);        my $b = \$a[0];   my $c = \delete $a[0];
      printf "array: ab=%d bc=%d\n", ($a==$b)?1:0, ($b==$c)?1:0; }
  perl: hash: ab=1 bc=1     array: ab=1 bc=1
  PCL : hash: ab=1 bc=0     array: ab=1 bc=0
  (`ab=1` on both sides is the control: PCL DOES give `\(values %h)` and
  `\$h{k}` the same identity, so element identity exists -- only the
  `delete` return value loses it.)

MECHANISM: `p-delete` removes the entry and returns the VALUE it read, so
`\` takes a reference to a fresh box.  perl's `delete` returns the removed
element's own SV, still addressable.  Fix area: `p-delete` in
`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` -- return the element's box.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md delete.t, "`\delete
$h{key}` address equality (tests 26, 54) ... PCL's delete returns a copy, not
the same slot."

FAMILY: `docs/not-supported.md` "Scalar copy does not preserve
reference/SV identity" -- but NOT registered there, because this one is a
discrete fixable slot, not the general copy semantics.
subject: BUG (SV identity): `\delete $h{k}` returns a ref to a COPY -- perl gives the same address as `\$h{k}` and `\(values %h)`, PCL gives a fresh box
